News.title: How millionaire TV exec was lured to his death in gruesome ‘honeytrap’ murder in shock act of ‘vigilante justice’
News.content:
LYING semi-conscious on the floor, millionaire TV station owner Gagandip Singh could do nothing as the blows rained down on him during a twenty minute punishment beating.

His only hope was that the medical student who had lured him to her bedroom in Brighton to be “taught a lesson” would hear his desperate cries for help.





But a new Channel 4 TV drama shows Mundill Mahil, 34, outside the door, blocking the path of a worried flatmate as a camera tripod struck Gagandip’s skull.

His cries of “Mundill, Mundill”, did not persuade her to intervene.

It is a deeply disturbing moment in a “honeytrap” murder case, which shocked the nation.

Having wrongly believed Gagandip died during the assault, his two attackers burned him alive in the back of a car on Blackheath in South London three hours later.



Mahil has always denied thinking that Gagandip, who she alleged had tried to rape her, would die.

But his relatives want the world to know the extent of the brutality meted out to the young entrepreneur.

Aysha Rafaele, the director of the C4 drama titled Vengeance: Murder On The Heath, reveals to The Sun: “When they were first told about the film, the family were really clear that they didn’t want me to underplay the violence that he had been subjected to.

“Having met Mundill and having met Gagandip’s family, obviously there’s a lot of anger on the side of the family still.”



The BAFTA award winning film maker followed the case when it unfolded 15 years ago.

The first reports were of a body being discovered in the boot of a Mercedes car, burned so badly that it was hard to know the make of vehicle.

Amandip Singh tried to identify the unrecognisable remains of her 21-year-old brother, but it needed a sample of his DNA to be certain.

Shortly afterwards, Mahil was charged with Gagandip’s murder, along with their friend Harinder ‘Ravi’ Shoker and a small-time criminal called Darren Peters.

What made the story even more heartbreaking was that Gagandip’s father Charanjit had been shot dead during a trip to India two years earlier.



It was an unimaginable double tragedy for Amandip and her mother Tejinder, from Bexleyheath, South London.

Sikh TV station owner Gagandip’s troubles began when he fell in love with the then 19-year-old Mahil, from Rochester, Kent, when she was studying to become a doctor at Brighton University.

Their mutual friend was Ravi, who also had a crush on Mahil.



According to the wannabe medic she never had any romantic feelings for either man.

And when Gagandip stayed over at her student digs he tried to rape her, pinning the teenager down on her bed before she managed to push him off.

He tearfully apologised and kept messaging Mahil, asking for forgiveness.

Both Ravi and another mutual friend called Sunny became aware of her distress and a plot was hatched.

Who initiated the plan and exactly what was intended is in dispute.



What is in no doubt is that it was Mahill who called Gagandip and invited him to visit her Brighton basement flat at 11pm on February 25 2011.

He was fearful enough about her possible intentions to ask in a text “OK, can we talk civil or do you just want me dead?”

Mahil claimed that she thought Sunny was just going to “mentor” Gagandip on how to treat women.

The problem with that version of events, is that a man called “Jason” turned up with Ravi rather than Sunny.

And Jason was really Darren Peters, who was a car thief.



As soon as Gagandip got through the bedroom door, the two men pounced on him and Mahil fled.

The two killers have been portrayed as “hitmen” defending the devout Sikh student’s “honour.”

Aysha does not believe that version of events, but is interested in the “vigilante justice” aspect of the case which she says is an issue in “our community.”

The British Pakistani Muslim film maker has a Punjabi background like some of the Sikh community involved in this story.

She explains: “When I first came across this story, it really sort of stayed with me, as I recognise a lot of the attitudes and the people and the psyche that might have ended up taking us to the place that it got to.



“I feel a lot of people from the Punjabi community will understand, there’s this sort of sense of trying to protect the honour of the women in your community.

“Maybe this is true of all types of society, but I particularly know it of my own one.”

Aysha read all the court transcripts and police interviews and spoke to the detectives, lawyers, Mahil and Tejinder.



She reveals: “I have met Mundill and talked her through everything that’s in the film.”

Having spoken to the honeytrapper and delved into the details of the case, Aysha has come to empathise with Mahil.

Aysha says: “I think she feels incredibly sad about the death of Gagan. And I think it’s devastated her life.”

In February 2012 a jury at the Old Bailey in London found Mahil not guilty of Gagandip’s murder, instead convicting her of causing grievous bodily harm.

She was jailed for six years, serving only half that sentence in jail.



Shoker, 34, will serve at least 22 years for murder and Peters, also 34, was jailed for 12 years for manslaughter.

The jury appeared to accept the argument put forward by Mahil’s barrister that she was not present when Gagandip was murdered.

Aysha continues: “Factually, he died, burnt alive in the car, many hours later, a great remove from her.

“She wasn’t in the room when he was getting attacked.

“I think what she failed to do was, and I think that she holds her hand up and says the regret that she heard him calling for her and didn’t do anything about it.



“Obviously, that is something that is undeniable.”

The Judge, Paul Worsley, seemed to believe a lot of the blame lay at Mahil’s door.

During sentencing he described her as “manipulative, vengeful and deceitful.”



For the director, Gagandip’s death was the result of a series of terrible decisions rather than a premeditated act.

She adds: “It feels like the worst decisions that the young people made then spiralled out of control, and wrecked lots of lives.”

It is Gagandip’s mother who has suffered the most.

Aysha says “To this day she has the double tragedy of living with the fact that not long before in 2009, her own husband had been murdered by a close friend on a business trip to India.”

Gagandip’s family think Mahil got off lightly.



Amandip and Tejinder campaigned for the attorney general to increase her prison sentence.

After she was released, Mahil married Varinder Singh Bola, who was elected as the mayor of Redbridge in London 2019.

He resigned as mayor before taking office, following outrage about his wife’s crime.

Mahil now works as a personal trainer and also helps other women who have been released from prison.

In 2020 Amandip said: “Mahil thinks that she can move on and leave everything that she’s done behind her, but I’m not going to let that happen because I will keep reminding people.”



Aysha told both Tejinder and Mahil what will be in the C4 drama, but she did not show them the finished film.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She concludes: “I hope that they will think that what I’ve done is a fair portrayal, and a sensitive portrayal.”

Vengeance: Murder on the Heath is on Channel 4 on May 24 at 9pm.

News.title: ‘Conspiracy theorist’ stepdad gave apocalyptic speech warning to ‘hide in nature’ days before abandoning kids in forest
News.content:
THE stepdad accused of abandoning two children in a Portuguese forest recorded strange videos just days earlier, warning people to hide in nature before the apocalypse.

Disturbing videos have emerged of Marc Ballabriga, 55, in which he says he is preparing for the end of the world.





Stepdad Ballabriga and Marine Rousseau, 41, are accused of abandoning their two children, Barthelemy and Zacharie, aged five and three, in a Portuguese forest, blindfolded in a twisted “treasure hunt” on May 19.

Just four days earlier, Ballabriga seems to have recorded the chilling videos which, as well as strange conspiracy theories, also contained hate speech, according to CNN Portugal.

He claimed to be speaking on May 15, and declared that the world would end on May 22, in the videos obtained by TVI.

Ballabriga, a former police officer said: “Today is the first day of the preparations for Armageddon, which will start on 22 May and which will last 28 days.

He added menacingly: “You will be afraid, you will all be afraid.

“Me, I won’t be afraid. I’ve been expecting this for a very long time.”

Ballabriga was arrested with his partner Rousseau on May 21.

The French couple were refused bail yesterday and will be held until their trial.



After warning of the end of the world, Ballabriga appears to tell people to hide in nature, where he says “there is enough space for us all”.

In the video, he declared: “We can hide, We can hide here between the rocks.

“We can all find solutions to find our shelter.”



In another clip, Ballabriga seems to believe he is in control of the sun, commanding it to shine in order to scare away a horse.

The horse, he claimed “is not natural, it was hybridised with reptile DNA“.

In another clip, Ballabriga turns the camera on himself to show his eyes, saying he has “no problem looking at the sun for a long time”.

Ballabriga and his partner Rousseau are thought to have told their five and three-year-old boys that they were playing a game called “drive away the devil”.

The boys were found crying and screaming alone on a rural road on Tuesday – before Rousseau, a sexologist, and her partner Ballabriga were tracked down by cops 100 miles away in a café near Lisbon.



The youngsters were said to be carrying a backpack packed with clothes, water, biscuits and fruit when they were found.



It comes as reports claimed the sexologist mum and ex-cop stepdad plotted to “pretend they were crazy” after their arrest.

Court officials are understood to be aware of the alleged conversation, that took place in a police car shortly after they were cuffed.

Bizarrely, Rousseau was heard belting out a song like an opera singer, while Ballabriga yelled in French: “I love you.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It is unclear who exactly Ballabriga was referring to when he made the remark.

A judge is expected to decide on Saturday whether the couple will be allowed to be released on bail.

News.title: BBC slammed for report on ‘Israeli genocide’ from £22-a-member group of ‘scholars’ where ANYONE can sign up & post views
News.content:
BEEB BLAST BBC slammed for report on ‘Israeli genocide’ from £22-a-member group of ‘scholars’ where ANYONE can sign up & post views

WHEN the BBC revealed that “leading scholars” declared Israel guilty of genocide, it sparked parliamentary debates and helped shape the views of the nation.

But the verdict presented to British audiences was, in reality, the opinion of roughly one fifth of the membership of a club you can join for the price of a trip to the cinema – with no qualifications needed. And now, after a global backlash, the membership list has quietly disappeared.





On September 1 last year, a single press release sent shockwaves through newsrooms across the world.

The International Association of Genocide Scholars (IAGS) had voted that Israel‘s actions in Gaza meet the legal definition of genocide.

The BBC ran with it instantly.

Their headline said: “Israel committing genocide in Gaza, world’s leading experts say.”



The Guardian followed. So did Reuters. In the UK, the framing landed hard, fuelling parliamentary debates, shaping public opinion and handing ammunition to campaigners calling for sanctions against Israel.

But nobody bothered to check who these “world’s leading experts” were.

The answer: anyone willing to hand over $30.

The Sun was able to enrol in the organisation despite making clear we are journalists and have no expertise in genocide.



The IAGS was founded in 1994 by serious academics who wanted genocide to be taken seriously as a field of study.

Its founders, including sociologist Helen Fein and Holocaust survivor Robert Melson, are names of genuine weight.

The organisation also publishes a peer-reviewed academic journal.



But the IAGS today operates an open-door membership model – with no credentials required, no background check and no verification of expertise.

You pick an income bracket, fill in your card details, and you are in.

The cheapest rate is $30 a year for those earning under $4,999, and no one checks what you earn.

When media watchdog Salo Aizenberg exposed the open membership policy in September 2025, others rapidly tested its limits.

Within hours, new members had joined under the names “Adolf Hitler“, “Emperor Palpatine” and “Cookie Monster”.



Dogs were registered and no one was turned away. The website buckled under the load.

Aizenberg had already found something more troubling – of roughly 600 members, at least 80 appeared to come from Iraq, a country with virtually no tradition of genocide scholarship and wildly over-represented in any serious academic body.

The resolution itself was passed on August 31 last year with a claimed 86 per cent in favour.

That sounds emphatic. But crunch the numbers and the picture changes dramatically.

Of some 500 members eligible to vote, only 28 per cent took part, which is around 140 people.



Of those, 86 per cent voted yes, meaning approximately 120 individuals.

The remaining 360 members abstained, did not vote, or were unaware.

The verdict that the BBC presented to British audiences as the considered judgement of “the world’s leading genocide scholars” was, in reality, the opinion of roughly one fifth of the membership of a club you can join for the price of a trip to the cinema.

The vote was anonymous and the names of the resolution’s authors were never disclosed.

A planned member meeting to discuss the controversy was cancelled and dissenting voices were blocked on the internal mailing list.



Prominent IAGS member Sara Brown has a PhD in comparative genocide studies from Clark University’s Strassler Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies.

She has researched genocide in Rwanda since 2004, authored a book on gender and the Rwandan genocide, and sat on the IAGS advisory board itself.

Her verdict on the Gaza resolution was withering. She called it reckless, poorly documented and based on deliberately skewed analysis.

Anyone who considers themselves a genocide scholar, she said, should be ashamed of this vote.

Notably, the resolution itself barely mentions Hamas.



The October 7 2023 attacks, in which over 1,200 people were murdered and 250 taken hostage, are dismissed in a single subordinate clause as “horrific” – with no analysis or condemnation.

The same body that in 2016 passed a detailed resolution on the genocidal crimes of ISIS managed just one word for Hamas.

None of this appeared in the BBC’s coverage. The corporation’s headline presented an institutional verdict as established fact.

Israeli diplomat Alex Gandler told The Sun: “The decision by outlets such as the BBC and others to amplify claims based on a deeply questionable organisation during an ongoing war was reckless and deeply damaging.

“By presenting these claims with insufficient scrutiny, major news organisations helped legitimise and spread the baseless and slanderous allegation of genocide as though it were an established scholarly consensus. Given the BBC’s reputation as a fair and neutral source of information, this had a cascading effect across international media coverage.



“This contributed to the continued spread of a false and highly inflammatory narrative during a time of conflict. The failure to fully and prominently correct or retract such reporting raises serious concerns regarding journalistic fairness, neutrality, and editorial responsibility.”

Eight months on, the IAGS website is fully operational.

The membership page is back. The subscribe buttons work. The fees are identical: $30 for the lowest earners, $125 at the top.

There are no credential checks and no verification processes.

The one thing that has changed: the public membership list is gone. Now, no one can now check who belongs to the organisation, how membership has shifted since October 7 2023, or whether a surge of new members influenced the vote.



The IAGS has heard the criticism, ditched the transparency, and kept the model.

A genocide declaration by a scholarly body carries real-world consequences.

It is cited in proceedings at the International Court of Justice, in UN reports, in parliamentary debates, and by NGOs whose conclusions in turn shape government policy.

In Britain, the BBC headline shaped how millions of people understood the conflict.

It was used in Commons debates. It was cited by activists and politicians alike.



The chain of authority that drove all of this began with a $30 subscription open to Cookie Monster.

Whether or not Israel is committing genocide in Gaza is a question for historians, lawyers and courts and the International Court of Justice is considering it.

But whether the IAGS has the authority to deliver that verdict on behalf of the scholarly community has been questioned.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And the BBC, by taking that claim at face value without checking the membership page that was sitting in plain sight, failed its audience at the most basic level.

The Sun has contacted the BBCand the IAGS for comment.

News.title: Moment tourist & mum-of-one is trampled to death after getting caught up in terrifying elephant fight
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a tourist was trampled to death during a vicious elephant fight in India.

Horrifying footage shows 33-year-old Tulasi get crushed beneath the front legs of one of the tusked titans while it thrashes on its side in a river.





The mum-of-one is submerged under the warring beasts as horrified onlookers try desperately to free her.

The Sun has decided not to show the full video as it is too distressing.

The woman’s husband managed to escape in the nick of time with their baby daughter in his arms, but was unable to help his wife.

A trainer riding the larger elephant appeared powerless to stop it from attacking its weaker rival.

The family had travelled from the coastal Indian city of Chennai for a two-day holiday.

Tulasi had been watching the animals being washed at the Dubare Elephant Camp in Coorg on May 18 when the fight broke out.

She had been standing nearby when one elephant charged without warning.

The weaker elephant was knocked to the floor and she became trapped underneath.



By the time the handlers managed to bring the elephants under control, the woman had died from her injuries.

The weaker elephant, a 34-year-old named Marthanda, died the following morning despite receiving treatment for her wounds.

In light of the incident, authorities have recommended a minimum 100ft distance between tourists and animals at elephant camps.

This means visitors will no longer be allowed to pose for photos with elephants or feed them.

Experts warn that even trained animals can display unpredictable behaviour.



It comes two months after a Brit tourist and her Kiwi cousin were trampled to death by a “peaceful looking” elephant at a safari.

Janet Taylor Easton, 67, from Bradford, and her cousin Alison Taylor, 67, from New Zealand, died in the terrifying attack in Zambia’s South Luangwa National Park.

The pair had been on a sunrise safari in the southern African nation in July last year.

During the tour, their group came upon an elephant and her calf.

According to guides, the beast first charged at Alison within a matter of seconds.



As the chaos ensued, guides fired shots at the charging elephant and wounded it in the process.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police say the guides were unable to stop the attack, which left both women dead.

An inquest heard the causes of death were traumatic thoracic injuries.

News.title: Mystery as son of Mango founder’s ‘phone he took on hike vanishes’ after billionaire dad plunged to his death
News.content:
MYSTERY is surrounding the disappearance of a mobile phone belonging to the son of Mango’s late founder who plunged to his death from a 150-metre cliff in Spain.

Among the evidence that turned Jonathan Andic from a grieving son into a suspect in fashion mogul Isak Andic’s death, is a missing iPhone 14 that the court is seeing as a red flag.





He is alleged to have had it with him when his father fell in the Montserrat park north of Barcelona, on December 14, 2024.

At the time, the two men were hiking together – and allegedly were trying to mend their relationship after a feud.

The phone was changed on March 26, 2025 – two weeks after the media reported on the reopening of the judicial case.

He has denied any involvement in his father’s death.

Jonathan alerted his secretary at Mango via WhatsApp that the mobile had been stolen during a 48-hour trip to Quito, Ecuador.

He requested a new one, an iPhone 16 Pro, which he activated as soon as he landed in Spain.

It was this coincidence that prompted police to verify the travel logs. And while the force confirmed that Jonathan did indeed fly to Ecuador, they found no record of the alleged loss of the phone.



They later discovered that the device was not even activated during the 48 hours, indicating that it might have been destroyed, sources familiar with the investigation told La Vanguardia.

They added that Jonathan could have used the business trip to dispose of it.

Judge Raquel Tierno Galván highlighted the “strange” circumstances in which the phone disappeared.

According to her ruling, Jonathan handed over the new mobile to police on September 9, when they requested it.

He further assured the police that it was “common” practice among senior Mango executives to periodically replace their phones for “security”.



He also denied any connection between the swaps and his father’s death.

On Tuesday, Jonathan posted an eye-watering £840,000 bail to avoid being remanded in jail.

A document released by the judge laid bare the alleged inconsistencies in his story – including how the father and son had a “bad relationship” and how Jonathan had an “obsession” with money.



It was also revealed that the son had allegedly scouted out the hiking route on three separate occasions before the day of his father’s death.

The document also cited police studies which showed the footprints on the ground where Isak plummeted to his death – which were allegedly not consistent with a simple slip.

Local cops said that “a rubbing action with the sole of the deceased’s shoes” was carried out “at least four times in both directions [forwards and backwards]” to create the type of footprint recorded on the mountain.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Galvan said: “From the investigative procedures carried out, it is concluded that there are sufficient indications to consider that the death of Mr. I. A. may have been a non-accidental death, with active and premeditated involvement in the death of his father by Mr. J. A.”

A spokesperson for the Andic family said the family is confident of Jonathan’s innocence and that he is cooperating fully with authorities.

News.title: Boy, 17, stabbed & nine people arrested after brawls erupt at massive gathering of youths in London as cops step in
News.content:
A TEENAGE boy has been stabbed and nine people arrested after mass brawls broke out at a huge gathering of feral youths in London.

Cops were scrambled to Clapham Common on Friday evening as violence erupted between swathes of teens in the capital.





Shocking footage posted on social media showed brutal fights breaking out at the “unauthorised gathering” in the popular South London park.

Yobs could be seen punching and fighting one another, with some even being targeted while lying on the floor.

A 17-year-old boy was later rushed to hospital with stab wounds, while nine people were arrested as chaos reigned down.

It comes just weeks after gangs of marauding teens tore through nearby Clapham High Street during so-called “linkups” fuelled by social media.



Shops including Waitrose, Sainsbury’s and McDonald’s were forced to close early as cops fought to bring the chaotic situation under control.

A huge police presence was also spotted at the park on Friday evening, after a music event reportedly spiralled out of control.

The situation worsened as officers armed with batons arrived on the scene and started dragging some of the youths away.

Screaming and shouting could be heard in the alarming clips shared online, as police scrambled to chase after the youths.



One video – titled “Clapham Courts” – showed hoards of teens squaring off with cops in chaotic scenes in the common.

Several ambulances could also be seen outside the entrance to the park.

The Met confirmed two teens, aged 14 and 16, were arrested for grievous bodily harm (GBH) and affray.



Four teenagers, aged between 16 and 19, were arrested for affray, while an 18-year-old man was arrested for assaulting a police officer.

A man, aged 20, and a boy, aged 15, were also arrested for possession of a knife.

The force said: “Police were called on Friday, 22 May to an unauthorised gathering on Clapham Common.

“The group were dispersed by officers after fighting broke out in the crowd, following this we made nine arrests.

“A 17-year-old boy was taken to hospital after he was found suffering with stab wounds.



“His injuries were assessed as neither life-changing nor life-threatening. All of those arrested remain in police custody.

“We urge anyone who was at the event or who has any information to come forward to police by calling 101 and quoting CAD8948/22May.

“A police presence will remain in the area, and we’ll be reviewing CCTV and other evidence in the coming days.”

Last month, brazen mobs caused chaos in Clapham High Street twice in a matter of days, after similar scenes were seen in Birmingham.

Clips circulating on social media showed mobs of teens gathering in the area with locals warning others to avoid the high street.



Flailing officers were heavily outnumbered by the vast swathes of youths – as they desperately tried to chase the youngsters away.

Thinus Keeve, retail director at M&S, later slammed London Mayor Sadiq Khan for failing to tackle crime in the capital.

He wrote: “I keep hearing crime is falling, especially in London… something none of us believes, and very few people working in retail would see.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Without a Government seriously cracking down on crime and a Mayor that prioritises effective policing, we are powerless.”

He also called on Labour to clamp down on shoplifting, revealing how staff had been headbutted and rushed to hospital following horrifying attacks.

News.title: Boy, 16, slashed across face with machete by two young men who fled on moped as cops launch manhunt
News.content:
BLADE HORROR Boy, 16, slashed across face with machete by two young men who fled on moped as cops launch manhunt

A TEENAGE boy has been left with serious injuries after he was slashed across the face with a machete by two young men on a moped.

Cops said the shocking attack happened on Saturday afternoon in Dudley, West Midlands, when the 16-year-old was walking in the area.





West Midlands Police say the teen was approached by two young men on a moped who attacked him with a machete before fleeing the scene.

The boy suffered serious injuries to his chest and face and has had to undergo surgery as a result.

Cops said they have recovered CCTV and mobile phone footage after launching an investigation.

They are now urgently appealing for help from the public to help them identify and arrest the suspects.

Extra patrols have also been put in place in the area today.

Det Insp Joe Davenport, from the force’s Major Crime Unit, said: “This was an horrific attack in the middle of the day and it could easily have resulted in this boy losing his life.

“We’ve been working tirelessly since then to understand exactly what happened, and who was responsible, and I’d urge anyone with information to get in touch with as soon as possible.”

News.title: Boy, 2, fighting for his life after plunging from window at house as cops launch probe
News.content:
HORROR FALL Boy, 2, fighting for his life after plunging from window at house as cops launch probe

A TW0-year-old boy is fighting for his life after plunging from a house window.

Emergency services raced to an address in Ashton-under-Lyne, Greater Manchester, on Saturday evening where the toddler was raced to hospital.





Greater Manchester Police said the boy had suffered life-threatening injuries from the fall, reports Manchester Evening News.

The force said that no arrests have been made as they launch an investigation into the horror incident.

Pictures show a large emergency service presence at the scene with an air-ambulance spotted landing the grounds of a church nearby.

The circumstances around the incident remain unclear but police are not treating it as suspicious.

A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said: “At around 5.40pm on Saturday, May 23, we were called to reports of a child falling from a window of house on Buttermere Road in Ashton-under-Lyne in Tameside.

“The child – a two-year-old boy – was taken to hospital with injuries that are described as life-threatening.



“No arrests have been made, and investigations are ongoing.”

The Sun has contacted North West Ambulance Service for comment.

News.title: Iran war live: Tehran declares it does NOT want nukes after peace deal progress
News.content:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country is ready to reassure the world it does not want a nuclear weapon, after Donald Trump said a peace deal was 'largely negotiated'

Iran war live: Tehran declares it does NOT want nukes after peace deal progress

Iran is ready to reassure the world it does not want a nuclear weapon, the country's president has announced.

However, Masoud Pezeshkian added that his country will not compromise when it comes to Tehran's 'honour and dignity'.

News.title: Belfast fire live: Titanic Quarter blaze seen for miles as locals told 'avoid area'
News.content:
Belfast Harbour Police and fire crews are currently at the Clearway industrial site in the Titanic Quarter as a massive plume of smoke can be seen for miles rising over the city

Belfast fire live: Titanic Quarter blaze seen for miles as locals told 'avoid area'

News.title: Nutrient-rich snack that may help with diabetes, heart health and ageing
News.content:
Nutrient-rich snack that may help with diabetes, heart health and ageing

The snack is packed with selenium and healthy fats that may support heart health, reduce inflammation linked to arthritis and diabetes, and boost skin elasticity – and just one or two a day could be enough

View 2 Images One snack secured 16th position in Healthline's list of 50 super healthy foods (Image: Miladin Pusicic via Getty Images)

There are numerous snacks packed with vitamins that can support the bodily changes you're aiming for. However, one particular snack stands out for its ability to aid thyroid function.

‌



Brazil nuts have secured 16th position in Healthline's list of 50 super healthy foods. The nut is described as: "nutrient-rich and have a smooth, buttery texture.

‌



The nutrients they contain support thyroid function, and they are a good source of the mineral selenium.

‌



Selenium is an essential trace mineral and brazil nuts are actually one of the best natural sources of it.

The mineral helps produce thyroid hormones and maintain metabolism.

Having just one to two brazil nuts a day can be enough to provide your daily selenium needs.

‌



Not only that, Brazil nuts are high in monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats, which support heart health.

This also reduced inflammation and help combat chronic inflammation linked to diseases like arthritis and diabetes. The benefits don't stop there, they also have omega-3 fatty acids which increases skin elasticity, reports Surrey Live.

View 2 Images Brazil nuts reduce inflammation and help combat chronic inflammation

‌



Munching on nuts could help slow the ageing process. Health guru Dr Michael Mosley has revealed that nuts are his main snack.

When asked by the Sunday Times about the food he eats every day, he said: "I make a point of always keeping a variety of nuts and seeds in stock, including almonds, cashews, Brazil nuts, walnuts, sunflower seeds, pine nuts, chia and sesame seeds.

"Nuts are rich in fibre to feed your microbiome and are an excellent source of healthy natural fat."

‌



If you're looking to add another nut to the mix, an expert has revealed the one nut he eats almost every day to make sure his heart stays healthy.

Dr Kevin Rabii, DO, FACC, a cardiologist with Memorial Hermann, told Parade that the foods we eat have an impact on developing risk factors for illnesses such as heart disease.

He explained that there is one nut he always keeps on hand as it's good for heart health.

Article continues below

"I enjoy almonds because they are an easy, healthy and delicious snack," he says. "I try to keep a small container with some almonds in my car or at work for when I am feeling hungry.

"There is no preparation involved, and it can keep you from choosing unhealthier snacks."

News.title: Legal rights explained when a neighbour’s BBQ smoke fills your garden
News.content:
Legal rights explained when a neighbour’s BBQ smoke fills your garden

Summer BBQs are the perfect occasions to bring the neighbourhood together, but they can also cause disputes

View 2 Images An active barbecue emits a lot of smoke (Image: Elva Etienne)

Nothing is more British than firing up the BBQ when scorching temperatures arrive over a bank holiday weekend. You might think it’s the sort of occasion that brings the whole neighbourhood together, but when thick smoke begins drifting over fences and through open windows, it can quickly spark tensions between neighbours.

‌



Most people have probably been there before - and on both sides of the fence too. Whether it’s neighbours complaining their washing now smells of smoke, struggling to breathe while relaxing outdoors, or becoming frustrated at clouds of fumes drifting through their homes, it can cause a right stir.

‌



Contrary to popular belief, there is no outright law banning barbecues in gardens or private outdoor spaces. However, excessive smoke, fumes or repeated disturbances could potentially amount to what councils call a 'statutory nuisance' in certain circumstances.

‌



Under GOV.UK guidance, local authorities can investigate complaints involving smoke, fumes and smells that unreasonably interfere with somebody's use or enjoyment of their property. Councils typically assess factors such as frequency, duration and severity before deciding whether further action is necessary.

Environmental health teams generally encourage neighbours to try resolving disputes informally before escalating complaints any further. In many cases, occasional BBQ smoke during warm weather is rarely to justify formal enforcement action on its own.

‌



View 2 Images A BBQ is a popular British summer pastime (Image: Getty Images)

Citizens Advice advises residents experiencing persistent nuisance problems to keep written records detailing dates, times and the impact on their property or wellbeing. Evidence such as photographs, videos or diary logs may also help support complaints if disputes continue.

Smoke can become more problematic for people with asthma or respiratory conditions, particularly during hot weather when windows and doors are left open. According to the NHS, smoke inhalation and poor air quality can worsen breathing difficulties and trigger symptoms in vulnerable people.

Article continues below

Meanwhile, local councils have powers under the Environmental Protection Act 1990 to investigate statutory nuisance complaints linked to smoke or fumes. If authorities determine a nuisance exists, they can issue an abatement notice ordering the problem to stop or be reduced.

Legal experts stress that every complaint is judged on its own individual facts and there is no automatic rule dictating how often somebody can use a barbecue. Occasional summer gatherings are generally considered part of normal day-to-day living, though excessive or persistent smoke affecting neighbouring properties could potentially cross the line.

Residents are also warned against retaliating against neighbours or deliberately escalating disputes. Mediation services are often recommended as a cheaper and less stressful way of resolving ongoing disagreements before they spiral further.

News.title: Wellness coach dies after ceremony 'using drug made from poisonous Amazon tree frog'
News.content:
Wellness coach dies after ceremony 'using drug made from poisonous Amazon tree frog'

A 40-year-old cancer survivor died after he is thought to have used a drug made from the poisonous skin of an Amazonian frog - his mum has called for it to be made illegal in the UK

View 2 Images Kristian Trend collapsed at home and later died in hospital (Image: FACEBOOK)

A British wellness coach and cancer survivor died after an apparent "detox" ceremony using a drug made from the deadly skin of a Amazonian tree frog.

‌



Kristian Trend, 40, is believed to have collapsed at his flat in Leicester after taking a drug known as Kambo, traditionally used in South America for fertility ceremonies and so-called purging. The drug is made from the poisonous dried skin secretions of the giant leaf frog. Kambo has been banned in many countries, including Australia and Chile, but is legal to purchase in the UK.

‌



The 40-year-old's mum, Angie, has called on the alternative medicine to be banned following the tragic death of her son, last month.

‌



View 2 Images The Kambo drug is made from the poisonous skin of a Amazonian tree frog (Image: Getty Images)

Kambo has been rising in popularity in Europe by people using the poisonous treatment as a wellbeing substance that could lead to "a life-changing experience".

Angie, speaking to The Telegraph, said her son was "very spiritual" and told her he was "going to cleanse himself", adding: "But I don’t know what happened."

‌



The heartbroken mum said: "We haven't had the test results back yet. I don’t know anything and I don’t even think I want to know what happened. It won’t bring him back."

Angie said her son spent had four months in hospital and nearly died while suffering from Burkitt lymphoma cancer but eventually recovered. On his cancer battle, Kristian previously wrote online: "At 23, I was given up to six months to live without intensive treatment. A rare cancer diagnosis forced me to choose: live in fear, or surrender to a higher purpose.

"After much travelling through India and Asia immersed in holistic wellness and meditation, the path became clear." The grieving mother added that his tragic death happened on his birthday week.

‌



While Kristian's cause of death has not been confirmed, if it is linked to Kambo he could be the first British victim of the drug. Leicestershire Police confirmed a man had been "taken unwell" at a home in Leicester on April 11 but later died in hospital.

Police added that a man, 41, was arrested on suspicion of administering poison. The force said the man was released on bail and an "investigation into the circumstances of the incident is continuing".

Kambo, also known as Sapo, has not been licensed by the UK and the Medicines and Healthcare Regulatory Agency as a medicine. The MHRA also does not regulate people who administer the alternative drug. Mum Angie called for the drug to be banned, saying: "I hope they ban it, but I'm not strong enough to fight for it. My husband died six years ago at 62. I’m completely lost now."

Article continues below

Kristian's family has set up a fundraiser in aid of the Loros hospice charity in Leicestershire. In a touching tribute they wrote: "For anyone who would like to make a donation in memory of Kristian. . . We would like to raise as much money as possible for such an amazing charity that meant the world to him and us as a family. Fly high big bro. We love you always, Mum, Kayla and Bligh."

The 40-year-old had recently launched a plant based energy drink named Feel Good Polys and his family plans to sell the remaining stocks and donated the money to charity.

The Home Office said it was working with health officials to monitor the substance. A spokesperson said: "Our thoughts are with Mr Trend’s family and loved ones. Any substance that poses a risk to public health or safety will be kept under review. We urge individuals to exercise caution when considering alternative therapies and to be aware of the potential risks involved."

News.title: Best foods to eat before bedtime to help you get a good night's sleep
News.content:
Best foods to eat before bedtime to help you get a good night's sleep

If you struggle to sleep, eating certain foods before bed could help you drift off more easily — a dietitian shares which sleep-promoting foods to eat, and which to avoid, for a better night's rest

View 3 Images Sometimes it can be hard to get a good rest and a full eight hours of sleep (Image: David Espejo via Getty Images)

Struggling to get a good night's sleep? An expert has revealed a handy tip that could help people lead a healthier lifestyle.

‌



The persistent problem of sleep deprivation affects one in three people in the UK, and beyond leaving you irritable the next morning, it's linked to serious health risks such as obesity, heart disease, and diabetes. It may come as a surprise that eating certain foods can actually encourage your body to unwind, helping people get the vital rest they need.

‌



Speaking to Express.co.uk in 2019, registered dietitian Rachel Clarkson shed light on the connection between nutrition and sleep: "Melatonin, a.k.a. the 'sleep hormone' is released by the brain to gently signal you to fall into a deep slumber, and the amount of melatonin released by your brain is actually dependent on the foods you eat."

‌



According to Rachel, amongst all the dietary influences on the body's melatonin production, there's a key protein component known as Tryptophan, reports Surrey Live.

View 3 Images Eggs are a great source of Tryptophan (Image: Getty Images)

She said: "This amino acid is classed as 'essential' in the diet because our bodies cannot make it and therefore it must be consumed from food."

‌



The following foods contain Tryptophan:

Fish

Eggs

Poultry

Spinach

Tofu

Beans

Lentils

Rachel added: "The science doesn't stop there because other nutrients actually affect whether Tryptophan is available in the body."

Both Magnesium and B vitamins regulate the availability of Tryptophan, which influences the sleep-inducing hormone melatonin and consequently affects how well a person sleeps.

‌



Foods containing Magnesium:

Nuts

Seeds

Milk

Cheese

Foods containing B vitamins:

Lentils

Soya

Spinach

Dairy

Fish

View 3 Images A cup of chamomile tea before bed may also prove beneficial (Image: Getty Images)

‌



According to the National Sleep Foundation, while certain foods can aid sleep, complex carbs have the opposite effect. People are advised to steer clear of white bread, refined pasta, and sugary treats before heading to bed, as these can reduce serotonin levels and disturb sleep, the NSA stated.

"Instead, choose stick-to-your-ribs whole grains for your bedtime snack: Popcorn, oatmeal, or whole-wheat crackers with nut butter are all good choices," the health organisation recommended. It's also suggested that the age-old tradition of enjoying a warm cup of milk could promote a better night's sleep, possibly owing to the tryptophan and melatonin found in milk.

The NSA added: "But perhaps more powerful is the psychological link between warm milk and bedtime as a child. Just like hot tea, a warm drink of milk can provide the perfect soothing backdrop for a relaxing bedtime routine."

Article continues below

Having a cup of chamomile tea before bed may also prove beneficial, potentially thanks to an antioxidant called apigenin, which chamomile tea is particularly rich in. This antioxidant has the ability to bind to brain receptors that may help reduce anxiety and promote sleep.

News.title: Woman, 19, hit by tram in Edinburgh and seriously injured as major road closed
News.content:
Woman, 19, hit by tram in Edinburgh and seriously injured as major road closed

Police have closed Leith Walk in Edinburgh after a woman was struck by a tram on Sunday morning - officers are appealing for help from the public

View Image A woman was struck by a tram in Edinburgh this morning (Image: EdinburghLive)

A road remains closed in Edinburgh after a woman was struck by a tram.

‌



Police are appealing for information after a 19-year-old woman was struck by a tram on Leith Walk at around 8.50am on Sunday.

‌



The incident happened between Albert Street and Pilrig Street near the Scotmid store. Emergency services attended and the woman was taken to the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh with serious injuries.

‌



One resident told The Record a woman had been seen carrying black bags to bins across the road when the incident happened.

The local, who wished to remain anonymous, went out to help with a first aid kit. They said: “It happened right outside my flat. The crowd had already put her in the recovery position when I got there.”

‌



Met Office forecasts 35C as weather maps show 18 counties hitting 34C – list READ MORE :

Arrest made in Eston 'murder' probe as man found dead and cops hunt second suspect READ MORE :

The road remains closed while crash investigation work is carried out. Sergeant Michael Thomson said: “Our inquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances and we are asking anyone who can help who has not already spoken to officers to get in touch.”

Edinburgh Trams said: "Due to an incident between McDonald Rd and Balfour St trams are running a part route service between Edinburgh Airport & St Andrew Sq only.

"Ticket acceptance in place with Lothian buses between St Andrew Sq - Newhaven. Apologies for any inconvenience caused."

Article continues below

Police Scotland said: "Leith Walk is closed from Duke Street to Iona Street following a report of a collision involving a pedestrian and a tram that happened around 9am on Sunday, 24 May.

"Road users are advised to avoid the area."

Lothian Buses confirmed services were being diverted from the area. They said on their site: "Due to a road closure buses are unable to serve Duke Street and Leith Walk and are instead diverted via London Road and Easter Road in both directions until further notice."

News.title: Saying goodbye to Football Focus after 52 years
News.content:
The final episode of Football Focus was broadcast on Sunday, bringing to an end 52 years on the air.

It was an emotional episode as long-time pundit Garth Crooks returned to Focus, sitting alongside Alex Scott to reflect on the show's past and preview the final day of the Premier League season.

Bob Wilson, the show's first presenter, closed out the programme by saying: "All good things come to an end. Thank you to all of you at home for watching Football Focus for the last 52 years. We have had a ball."

Launched in 1974, Football Focus provided fans with interviews, analysis and stories from across the game every lunchtime before the weekend's fixtures begin.

The longest-running magazine show in the world began with a tribute to the programme, with its former presenters sharing their favourite memories from across the decades.

The programme's old branding was used throughout in a nod to its history.

Crooks ended the show by presenting Scott with a picture of herself and Bob Wilson, on behalf of the "Football Focus family".

Before handing over to Wilson, an emotional Scott said: "For 52 years, this show has done one thing. Week in, week out, it has brought football into your Saturday afternoons. Whether it was Bob Wilson or any of the brilliant people who sat in this chair after him, the thing that never changed was you - the fans.

"I won't pretend this isn't hard. What I know is, the football doesn't stop, the stories don't stop. The goals, the drama, the heartbreak, the magic, none of that stops. It just finds a new home.

"From everyone who has ever worked on Football Focus, thank you. Thank you for making Saturday lunchtime something to look forward to. It has been an honour."

The Kyiv region was pounded with hundreds of drones and missiles overnight and into Sunday in a mass bombardment of Ukraine’s capital and surrounding area.

The fatal attack came after Vladimir Putin vowed to retaliate for the strikes on a student dormitory on Friday.

Russia struck the region with a powerful Oreshnik hypersonic intermediate-range ballistic missile, which Putin has claimed is immune to any missile defence system.

At least four people have died, and more than 80 have been injured in the attack, which targeted multiple structures, including residential buildings and schools.

open image in gallery Rescuers operate at the site of a heavily damaged building as smoke rises following Russian strikes in Kyiv ( AFP/Getty )

Russia launched 600 strike drones and 90 air, sea and ground-launched missiles, with Ukrainian air defences destroying and jamming 549 drones and 55 missiles.

Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the attack, calling the Russian leader “unhinged”.

He wrote on X: “Putin can’t even pronounce the word ‘hurrah’ clearly anymore – slurs and mumbles – yet he is still vanquishing residential buildings with his missiles. Launched three Russian missiles against a water supply facility. Burned down a market. Damaged dozens of residential buildings. Hit several ordinary schools. Launched his “Oreshnik” against Bila Tserkva.

“They really are unhinged. It is important that this does not pass without consequences for Russia.”

The head of Kyiv’s military administration said damage was recorded in 40 locations across several districts of the capital, as fire raged into the morning.

It comes after Putin denounced the drone strike on a college dormitory in Starobilsk, in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine, which Moscow says killed 21 people and injured 42.

open image in gallery Red Cross volunteers carry an injured woman into an ambulance after a Russian strike on a residential neighborhood ( AP )

The Russian leader blamed the strike on Kyiv on Friday and ordered his military to submit its proposals for retaliation.

However, Ukraine has denied targeting the dorm, saying it had struck an elite drone command unit in the area.

At a UN Security Council emergency meeting held at the request of Russia, Ukrainian ambassador Andrii Melnyk rejected his Russian counterpart’s accusations of war crimes, calling them a “pure propaganda show”. He said Friday’s operations “exclusively targeted the Russian war machine.”

Russia’s overnight attack targeted a five-story residential building, which was hit in Kyiv’s Shevchenko district, causing a fire and killing one person.

A school building that had people sheltering inside was also damaged, according to mayor Vitalii Klitschko. Local authorities reported that supermarkets and warehouses across the city were also hit.

Kyiv resident Svitlana Onofryichuk, 55, who has worked in a market that was damaged, said the large-scale attack meant she would likely have to relocate.

open image in gallery A fragment of a Russian Oreshnik intermediate range hypersonic ballistic missile that hit the Lviv region in January ( AP )

“It was a terrible night, and there had never been anything like it in the entire war.

“I am very sorry that I have to say goodbye to Kyiv now, I am not staying there anymore, there is no possibility," she added. “My job is gone, everything is gone, everything has burned down.”

The European Union’s foreign policy chief said the attack was a display of “reckless nuclear-brinkmanship”.

Kaja Kallas said: “Russia hit a dead-end on the battlefield, so it terrorises Ukraine with deliberate strikes on city centres. These are abhorrent acts of terror meant to kill as many civilians as possible.

“Moscow reportedly using Oreshnik intermediate-range ballistic missiles – systems designed to carry nuclear warheads – is a political scare-tactic and reckless nuclear-brinkmanship.”

Ms Kallas said foreign ministers would discuss how to “dial up the international pressure on Russia.”

open image in gallery A Ukrainian firefighter operates at the site of a heavily damaged shopping centre as smoke rises in the background ( AFP/Getty )

World leaders have criticised the attack, with German chancellor Friedrich Merz hitting out at Russia’s use of the Oreshnik missile system.

“The German government strongly condemns this reckless escalation. Germany continues to stand firmly by Ukraine,” he wrote on X.

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney said Russia was “prolonging human suffering and doing nothing to change the fact that Russia will lose this war.”

Russia has already attacked ‌Ukraine twice with the Oreshnik missiles, targeting the Ukrainian city of Dnipro in November 2024 and the western Lviv region in January. Putin has boasted that the missile streaks at 10 times the speed of sound.

Home player Arthur Gea ran off the court for an emergency bathroom break early in the first set of his French Open debut on Sunday.

“I need to go to the bathroom. I can’t move anymore. I’m going to (go) on the court,” Gea told the chair umpire in French before hastily running off Court Suzanne-Lenglen.

The 135th-ranked Gea was trailing 13th-seeded Karen Khachanov 4-2 when he made his move. Khachanov won 6-3, 7-6 (3), 6-0.

Usually, bathroom breaks are only permitted between sets.

Khachanov protested to the chair umpire as three minutes passed between games at a point in the match that was not a changeover when players change ends.

Gea said the umpire allowed him the break because of "medical circumstances" and that he was given some medicine to settle his stomach pain.

After the match, Gea said he had not felt ill the night before but started feeling unwell when he woke up in the morning.

“During the match it was even worse,” he said. “I had to go to the toilet really quick.”

His situation was not helped by the intense heat at Roland Garros with lunchtime temperatures hitting 31 degrees Celsius (88 Fahrenheit).

“It was harder than usual, because I was ill,” he said.

The 21-year-old Gea received a wild card invitation from Roland Garros organizers to participate in the main draw.

Arson attacks on Ebola treatment centers in eastern Congo show how authorities are faced with a number of serious complications — including a backlash in local communities — as they try to stop an outbreak of an infectious disease that has been declared a global health emergency.

The burning of the centers in two towns at the heart of the outbreak shows the anger in a region beset by violence linked to armed rebel groups, the displacement of a large number of people, the failure of local government and international aid cuts that experts say have stripped health facilities in vulnerable communities.

“A devastating set of emergencies are converging," said the Physicians for Human Rights nonprofit.

Here's a look at the longstanding crises in eastern Congo that have made it home to one of the world's worst humanitarian disasters, and how they are now affecting the response to a rare type of Ebola:

The region has a constant threat of violence

Eastern Congo has seen violence by dozens of separate rebel groups for years, some of them with links to foreign countries or Islamic State.

The Rwanda-backed M23 rebels are in control of parts of the region. While the Congolese government still largely controls the northeastern Ituri Province, which is the epicenter of the Ebola outbreak, that control is tenuous. The Allied Democratic Forces, a Ugandan Islamist group linked to Islamic State, is one of the dominant rebel groups there and responsible for violent attacks against civilian targets.

Before the outbreak, Doctors Without Borders said in an assessment of the situation in Ituri that the insecurity had worsened recently, causing doctors and nurses to flee and leaving overwhelmed health facilities and “catastrophic” conditions in some parts.

Nearly a million people are displaced in Ituri

Nearly 1 million people in Ituri have been displaced from their homes by conflict, according to the United Nations humanitarian office.

That means this Ebola outbreak is “unfolding in communities already facing insecurity, displacement and fragile health care systems,” said Gabriela Arenas, Regional Operations Coordinator at the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

It's a significant concern that the disease might spread to the large displacement camps near the city of Bunia, where the first cases were reported.

Authorities have announced more than 700 suspected Ebola cases and more than 170 suspected deaths, mostly in Ituri. But cases have been reported in two other eastern provinces, North Kivu and South Kivu, where M23 are in control, and also in the neighboring country of Uganda.

That means that part of the outbreak in Congo is being managed by the government and part by rebel authorities, with an array of aid agencies also helping.

Aid cuts were devastating for eastern Congo

Health experts say international aid cuts last year by the United States and other rich nations were devastating for eastern Congo because it has so many problems.

The cuts “reduced the capacity to detect and respond to infectious disease outbreaks,” said Thomas McHale, public health director at Physicians for Human Rights. Congo has had more than a dozen previous Ebola outbreaks.

Aid groups fighting this outbreak on the ground say they don't have the equipment they need, like face shields and suits to protect health workers from infection, testing kits, and body bags and other materials needed to safely dispose of the bodies of victims, which can be highly contagious.

“We have made requests to different partners, but we have not yet really received anything,” said Julienne Lusenge, president of Women’s Solidarity for Inclusive Peace and Development, an aid group operating a small hospital near Bunia.

“We only have hand sanitizer and a few masks for the nurses.”

The Bundibugyo type of Ebola virus responsible for the outbreak has no approved vaccine or treatment.

Health and aid workers also face anger from local communities

The burning of two treatment centers by people in the Rwampara and Mongbwalu areas — which have the highest case counts — show how a backlash in some communities is further complicating the response.

Colin Thomas-Jensen, director of impact at the Aurora Humanitarian Initiative, said the attacks may reflect the “built-in skepticism and anger” of people in eastern Congo over how the region has been treated, with years of violence from foreign-linked rebel groups and a failure of their government and international peacekeepers to protect them, he said.

Another source of anger has been the strict protocols around the burial of suspected victims of Ebola, which authorities are taking charge of wherever they can to prevent further spread of the disease when families prepare the bodies and people gather for a funeral.

The first burning of an Ebola center in Rwampara was by a group of local youths trying to retrieve the body of a friend who died, according to witnesses and police. The witnesses said the crowd accused the foreign aid group operating there of lying about Ebola.

Authorities in northeastern Congo have now banned funeral wakes and gatherings of more than 50 people in an effort to curb the spread, and armed soldiers and police are guarding some burials carried out by aid workers.

AP writers Mark Banchereau and Wilson McMakin contributed to this report.

News.title: Russell takes last-gasp pole after clashing with Antonelli in Canada sprint
News.content:
Antonelli was told to calm down by race engineer Peter “Bono” Bonnington after his outburst over the radio after the first incident. But when he carried on complaining, he earned a rebuke from his team principal Toto Wolff, who told him to “concentrate on the driving”.

Then, at the end of the race, after Antonelli went off track a third time trying to pass Norris and was looking to vent his spleen again on the cool-down lap, Wolff shut him down a second time. “Kimi, now is not the time to talk about this. We will talk about this later, not on the radio.”

The two Mercedes men had a brief handshake after getting out of their cars, but it promised to be an awkward debrief.

Sky Sports F1 pundit Martin Brundle said it was no surprise to see the two come to blows given they are fighting for the title. Russell is under pressure this weekend because Antonelli has won the last three races to take the championship lead.

“It was always going to happen. Inevitable. Kimi lost his head a little bit but he’ll learn from this,” was Brundle’s verdict.

The fighting at the front was the highlight of an entertaining sprint race in general. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton looked as if he would take fourth spot for most of the race, only to clip the “Wall of Champions” late in the race. Hamilton was then passed by McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, losing position, which allowed Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc to pass him as well.

News.title: Oli McBurnie spies £200m tap-in to fire unlikely lads Hull to Premier League
News.content:
This is a manager and squad that have fostered an admirable team spirit, although they now find themselves in late May staring up at a challenge on a completely different scale to that which came before. At the very least one could say that they have acclimatised to playing without the ball. Jakirovic also looks like a quick learner – epitomised by his record against Middlesbrough this season. Hull were 4-0 down to Boro at home in early December and eventually lost 4-1, but won at the Riverside Stadium at the end of the month.

The Boro manager Kim Hellberg acknowledged that his players had not been “sharp enough” to create the chances their domination of the ball might have warranted. Their year has taken some turns. The manager they sacked one year ago is now in charge of Manchester United on a two-year contract. Michael Carrick’s successor Rob Edwards is back in the Championship with Wolverhampton Wanderers. Boro’s best player, Hayden Hackney, will now assume – for the second time this month – that he has played his last game for the club.

Hackney, 23, the hometown hero, came off the bench in the second half having not played since March 14 with a calf injury. Having watched the play-off semi-final defeat to Southampton he will have thought that was the end. It certainly is now with Premier League clubs circling, and Crystal Palace thought to be the likely destination. There were fine performances from the US international Aidan Morris in midfield and Luke Ayling at centre-back, and both had plenty of the ball. They just found it impossible to create a chance.

Both teams would have required major changes to be competitive in the Premier League and for Hull, back from the brink of League One, it is a giant step up. They can enjoy their day of triumph but the next 38 league games will be the test of their lives.

News.title: How to have a happy dog and other tips from vets, breeders and trainers
News.content:
Perhaps your dog is easily agitated and you’ve never been able to understand why. According to Dr Wedderburn, the answer might be – and don’t laugh – childhood trauma. “Many, many dogs these days are reactive and get anxious in new situations,” he explains. “They get aggressive and fearful, which is often because they’re badly socialised when they’re young.”

“Puppies have a socialisation window in their brain up until four months of age,” Dr Wedderburn says. “Whenever they come across a new experience, their brain will accept it as being part of the normal world. If they don’t meet experiences until they’re older than that, until they’re maybe five or six months of age, then their brain is fearful and anxious instead and they retain that fear and anxiety for the rest of their lives.”

Trainer Cox has plenty of experience dealing with anxious dogs: “The most important thing is to recognise that the dog is overstimulated and remove them from that environment. Some dogs like gentle stroking, others like a quiet, calm voice or soft food or something else to chew. Maybe a snuffle mat that they can do a little bit of sniffy work – that tends to take their arousal levels down.”

News.title: Leinster humiliated as ruthless Bordeaux retain Champions Cup crown
News.content:
This time there was no Champions Cup final heartbreak for Leinster, just humiliation. In their previous four defeats at the final reckoning, the Irish province could look agonisingly to key moments when the pursuit of a fifth star fell just short.

But this was different. This time there could be no gnashing of teeth, no looking back ruefully at squandered opportunities. This time they came up alarmingly short against a Bordeaux-Bègles side who have, in the eight years since Leinster won the last of their Champions Cup crowns, established themselves as the new European superpower.

The manner in which they retained their title was, quite simply stunning, with all the damage done in a first half that yielded five converted tries, finished by their outstanding captain, Maxime Lucu, Pablo Uberti, Louis Bielle-Biarrey (2) and Yoram Moefana.

They have not lost a Champions Cup game since being beaten by Harlequins in the quarter-finals during the 2023-24 season. The arrival of Tom Willis from Saracens will only strengthen their hand.

News.title: Uganda confirms three more Ebola cases
News.content:
Uganda has confirmed three more Ebola cases as the burgeoning outbreak from neighbouring Congo continues to spread.

Health officials said the new cases brought the total detected in Uganda to five.

Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remains the epicentre of the outbreak but the World Health Organization warned there was a high risk of the infection spreading to other east African countries.

A week after the outbreak was first confirmed, DRC authorities reported that the flare-up was already the third largest on record, with 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.

Relief efforts are being hampered by insecurity in Ituri and the fact the outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, rather than the Zaire strain, which caused 15 of the DRC’s previous 17 outbreaks. There are no approved vaccines for the variant, which can kill up to half of those it infects.

News.title: How to get a good night’s sleep when it’s hot and light outside
News.content:
There are plenty of reasons to celebrate a heatwave, but a good night’s sleep is probably not one of them.

You toss and turn, flipping the pillow over and over to try to find the cool side, coated in a sticky sheen of sweat. And the extra daylight is a mixed blessing, making it harder to drop off and trickier to stay asleep once we do.

Light evenings tend to reset our body clock that’s located in our brain. Unfortunately, this is exactly the type we need to feel rested in the morning.

“Our sleep cycle is governed by our sense of light and dark, or circadian rhythm,” explains Dr Guy Meadows, the co-founder and clinical director of the Sleep School app.

The longer we see light, the longer our in internal clock tells our body it is daytime and needs to stay alert. When it gets dark, the body clock signals that it’s time to sleep by releasing melatonin. In summer months we secrete less melatonin, which one reason we wake up earlier and find it harder to drop off.

Temperature is another incredibly important facet of falling asleep, explains Dr Meadows. “Our core body temperature plays an important role in the regulation of sleep. At the start of the night, a 1C drop in temperature is needed to help you fall asleep,” he says. “It’s this decrease, coupled with the arrival of darkness, that informs the internal body clock that the night has begun. This triggers the release of the sleeping hormone melatonin, helping you fall asleep.”

Here, Dr Meadows shares his top tips to sleep in the light and heat:

1. Reduce your exposure to light before preparing for bed

Reducing light use before you head to bed is important, Dr Meadows says. So resist the urge to bask in the evening light.

Draw your blinds to dim the light a good couple of hours before you’re ready to turn in, so that your body begins to step up melatonin production. And don’t forget to switch off electronic devices.

You might also want to invest in blackout blinds – John Lewis do a good range – or at least a sleep mask. Look for masks with adjustable straps that will stay in place and deliver a comfortable, full-blackout.

2. Keep your head cool by keeping a cool head

Dr Meadows adds: “Getting frustrated and restless because you’re too warm only makes your body generate more heat, keeping you awake for longer. Keep cool by lying still and accepting the heat.

“Try focusing your attention on the discomfort and describe what you feel objectively and without judgement, such as ‘I feel heat and sweat on my face, neck and back’. Learning to change your relationship with the heat helps defuse its power and lead to better sleep.”

3. Prepare for cooler sleeping during the daytime

It might sound counter-intuitive, but keeping your curtains closed can stop your bedroom getting warm in the first place, making it easier to fall asleep at night. Another thing to do is to avoid a late dinner.

“Eating food close to bedtime elevates your body temperature, making it harder to sleep,” says Dr Meadows. “For the best night’s sleep, leave at least two hours between eating and sleeping – and limit alcohol consumption.”

4. Wear cotton pyjamas or sleep naked

“If you’re wearing natural fibres like cotton, then you’ll feel cooler in the night than if you were naked, because the cotton will wick away sweat from your skin,” says Dr Alanna Hare, an NHS and private sleep consultant at the Royal Brompton Hospital.

“However, anything man-made or synthetic will keep heat next to your skin. And the same goes for bedding. So if I had the choice between cotton and nakedness, I’d choose cotton. But if you’re choosing between man-made fibres and nakedness, go naked.”

5. Create a breeze

“Sleep with the window open or keep a fan on during the night to add an extra breeze in your bedroom,” Dr Meadows advises.

If you want to keep things extra cool, place a frozen bottle of water between yourself and the fan to cool the air as it comes towards you. (Modern air coolers can chill the room by a few degrees using this principle, although they’re not as effective as refrigerating air conditioners.)

6. Make a ‘cold water bottle’

“Simply fill a hot water bottle with cold water and keep it in the fridge or freezer for a few hours before bed – if you’re an extra hot sleeper, you can leave it in a little longer,” suggests Chris Tattersall, a sleep expert at bedding manufacturer Woolroom.

“Then snuggle up with your ice pack under the covers or leave it to cool down the bed before jumping in – it’s one of the best ways to keep cool at night.”

7. Ditch the memory foam

“The synthetic materials used in a memory foam mattress mean that it’s not breathable and doesn’t absorb moisture, leaving your body to overheat and sweat while in bed,” says Tattersall.

“You know that sinking feeling you get when you sleep on a memory foam mattress? For that to happen, it needs body heat to warm it up, which is then reflected back onto you as you sleep.

“Overlaying your memory foam mattress with a wool mattress protector will help regulate around 75 per cent of that heat, helping you stay cooler on those hot summer evenings.”

Sports.title: Leicester release ten players including FOUR ex-Premier League stars and an FA Cup winner after drop down to League One
Sports.content:
LEICESTER CITY have released ten players including four ex-Premier League stars following their embarrassing relegation to League One.

The Foxes endured another pathetic campaign, which included the first points deduction in their history, to suffer back-to-back drops.





And after their dismal Championship campaign, the club has let a host of the flops go.

That includes captain Ricardo Pereira.

Pereira, 32, announced his exit before the final game of the season and departs after eight years at the King Power.

The seven-cap Portugal international was one of the top right-backs in the Premier League and was part of the Leicester team that won the FA Cup in 2021.



He made 220 appearances for the club but suffered a series of serious, long-term injuries.

Fellow former Prem men Patson Daka, Jordan Ayew and Jamaal Lascelles have all been released, too, after failing to keep the Foxes up.

Leicester spent £23million on Daka but, despite a four-goal blitz against Spartak Moscow in October 2021, he struggled for goals and leaves with 29 in 165 games across five seasons.

Ayew joined at the beginning of the 2024-25 season but only managed 12 goals in 80 appearances.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Lascelles, meanwhile, only played nine times for the club after penning a short-term deal from Newcastle in February.

Academy graduate Wanya Marcal’s contract is also up.

Youth-team players Jake Donohue, Jahmari Lindsay, Alfie Fisken, Toby Onanaye, Olaoluwa Omobolaji and Chris Popov have all been released.

Loanees Jordan James, Aaron Ramsey, Joe Aribo, Dujuan Richards and Divine Mukasa will now return to their parent clubs after mixed success.

James was crowned the club player of the year and the Championship young player of the year.



Veteran goalkeeper Asmir Begovic’s deal also expires at the end of the season.

However, the club confirmed he is still in negotiations over an extension.

Leicester have offered new deals to Stevie Bausor, Harry French, Mirsad Ali, Bobby Amartey, Silko Thomas, Logan Briggs and Josh King.

Five academy players – Henry Cartwright, Tommy Neale, Ryan Donnelly, Thomas Wilson-Brown and Reiss Khela – have already put pen to paper to stay in the East Midlands.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker’s shock BBC replacement for historic World Cup final set to be revealed
Sports.content:
GABBY LOGAN will reportedly replace Gary Lineker and present the World Cup final on the BBC.

And that will see her become the Beeb’s first female host of the biggest game in football.





Logan, Kelly Cates and Mark Chapman are sharing the main presenting duties through the tournament – just as they have done on Match of the Day.

But with Lineker stepping aside last year after covering all the World Cups from 2002 to 2022, the primary slot of the final is up for grabs.

Now, though, the Daily Mail report Logan is in pole position to get the gig.

That is partly because Chapman is expected to return to the UK to cover The Open golf.



The final round of the final major of the season is on Sunday 19 July, the same day as the World Cup final.

Logan will already make history by becoming the first woman to front an England men’s World Cup game for the BBC.

She will be in the hotseat for the clash with Ghana in Boston on June 23.

However, the majority of the BBC’s coverage of the 104-match, five-week tournament is set to stay in the studios in Salford.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They are then expected to send a crew out to North America for the closing stages.

ITV have the rights to England’s opener against Croatia and their Group L finale with Panama.



They will be based in New York City for the duration of the World Cup, with their rooftop studio offering stunning views across to Manhattan and the Brooklyn Bridge.

Both broadcasters have now revealed their full punditry line-ups.

Thomas Frank, Olivier Giroud, Cesar Azpilicueta, Theo Walcott and Gael Clichy join BBC regulars Alan Shearer, Micah Richards, Wayne Rooney and Joe Hart.

ITV’s squad, meanwhile, includes Juan Mata, Ange Postecoglou, Patrick Vieira, Gary Neville, Ian Wright and Roy Keane.

SunSport has contacted the BBC for clarity on the decision over the final.

Sports.title: International footballer rushed to hospital in critical condition for emergency surgery after crashing motorbike
Sports.content:
tragic International footballer rushed to hospital in critical condition for emergency surgery after crashing motorbike

FORMER Greek international defender Marios Oikonomou has suffered a serious motorbike accident in his hometown of Ioannina.

The 33-year-old, who only retired from the game in 2024, is said to have crashed into the car of a 63-year-old man right in front of the

Hatzikosta hospital.





According to reports, the six-time Greek international suffered serious head injuries and he underwent emergency surgery.

He has subsequently been transferred to intensive care at Ioannina University Hospital.

It is not yet known how critical his condition is.

Authorities have also said the circumstances of the accident remain under investigation.

Some of Oikonomou’s former clubs have taken to social media to offer their support at this difficult time.

AEK Athens said in a statement: “The AEK Athens family stands by Marios and his family, with the hope that he can emerge victorious from the most difficult battle of his life.”

Bologna wrote on social media: “Come on Marios, we are all with you.”

Oikonomou spent a large part of his career in Italy, gracing Serie A with Bologna, Cagliari and his last club in the division, Sampdoria.



As well as his adventures in Italy, the 6ft 2in centre-back also played in the Danish rop-flight with Copenhagen and returned home to Greece to play for AEK Athens.

He finished his career around 90 miles away from where he was born with Panetolikos.

Sports.title: ‘Retiring where I belong’ – Premier League title winner, 39, quits football after leading side back to Champions League
Sports.content:
FORMER Liverpool goalkeeper Adrian has called time on his career at his boyhood club Real Betis.

The 39-year-old has decided to hang up his gloves after a 345-game career that included 11 years in England.





The Spaniard collected a Premier League winner’s medal in 2019/20 after playing eleven times for the Reds that season, but he departed Anfield in 2024 to return home.

Born and raised in Seville, Adrian had the pleasure of starting and finishing his career at his local club.

But to make the moment even more special, he was able to help his beloved Betis secure the fifth and final Champions League spot in La Liga.

He said: “From that little boy who started playing a long time ago, at just 10 years old; in the end, life makes you experience moments and decisions.



“Returning home two seasons ago, experiencing wonderful things, which is why I came back; it was the right time, I felt it in my heart.

“What could be better than playing here today in front of my fans, my people, my family; it’s an honor.

“I only have words of gratitude for Real Betis because they gave me everything from the beginning, from when Adrián started his career.
